---
title: "How to analyse a grid of rating questions"
description: "Summarise the ratings for each row of a grid question and compare them between groups."
---

Summarise the ratings for each row of a grid question and compare them between groups.

The example in this guide is *Rate each session*. A course evaluation in which students rate each part of a course on one grid, compared across students who attended in person and online.

## In SurveyStudio

1. In RStudio, open the **Addins** menu, choose **surveyframe: Try a demo** and pick `matrix_likert`.
2. On **Design**, select the grid. Each row becomes its own column in the data, named after the row.
3. On **Explore**, view the distribution of ratings for each row.
4. On **Analyse**, run the descriptives for every row and the cross-tabulation of 1 row by attendance format.

![The Design screen with the Rate each session study open.](../../templates/matrix_likert/design.png){width=100%}

## In R

```r
d <- sframe_demo("matrix_likert")
names(d$responses)                  # 1 column per grid row
results <- run_analysis_plan(d$responses, d$instrument)
```

## The research questions and what the report gives

| Research question | Method | What the report gives |
|---|---|---|
| How was each part of the course rated? | Descriptive statistics | The APA 7 sentence and a table, with a chart where the method has one |
| How were ratings of the lectures distributed? | Frequencies and percentages | The APA 7 sentence and a table, with a chart where the method has one |
| Did in-person and online students rate the lectures differently? | Cross-tabulation | The APA 7 sentence and a table, with a chart where the method has one |

Run the example in SurveyStudio or R to see the results, each marked as demonstration data.
